item.title: Saudi Arabia says Houthis tried to attack its capital
item.description: Saudi Arabia on Saturday said that Yemen's Houthi rebels tried to attack Riyadh with a ballistic missile, the first time the Saudi capital has been targeted since the escalation in fighting with the Iran-backed rebels opened a new front in the Iran war.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico reporters denied access to White House following Trump ban
item.description: Three reporters were blocked from the White House grounds Saturday morning, a day after President Trump said CNN, Politico, and MS NOW would be banned for reporting "FICTION and LIES."

item.title: Trump says he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House
item.description: The president chalked the ban up to what he called unfavorable coverage, and he threatened that bans on other media companies could be coming.

item.title: White House withdraws nomination of Lance Schroyer to lead ICE
item.description: President Trump's nominee to lead U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement was former Oklahoma state trooper Lance Schroyer. Three months after tapping him for the job, his name is being withdrawn.

item.title: Republican 'cavalry' arrives with a Trump-backed $150 million ad blitz in key races
item.description: To counter a difficult political environment, two Trump-aligned super PACs have reserved more than $150 million in ads — primarily in deep red House and Senate races that have now become competitive.

item.title: A DHS email raises new questions about the Trump administration's election plans
item.description: A heavily redacted email from last year, reported first by NPR, reveals that DHS personnel shared a list of jurisdictions that offer election materials in non-English languages. It's unclear why.

item.title: Some GOP candidates are still making election fraud claims. Voters want to move on
item.description: President Trump and some Republican battleground candidates are still embracing false claims about widespread election fraud in 2020, even as many GOP voters want them to move on.
